intro.title: Longest Ones with K Flips
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that finds the longest subarray of 1s in a binary array, allowing you to flip up to K zeros to 1s. You will learn the sliding window technique, a core algorithm pattern for efficiently solving array problems. The implementation will use basic JavaScript constructs like arrays, loops, and conditional logic. By the end, you'll understand how to track a window and adjust it dynamically to maximize the length of consecutive 1s.
intro.usecase: The Longest Ones with K Flips algorithm is essential for optimizing data streaming and signal processing in real-time applications. It's commonly used in network monitoring dashboards to identify the longest consecutive sequence of successful data packets, allowing engineers to detect stable connection periods. In video streaming services, this pattern helps analyze buffering sequences to determine optimal quality settings while maintaining smooth playback. Financial trading platforms apply similar logic to track consecutive profitable trades within risk tolerance limits, helping traders identify reliable market trends.
